subtitle: Lesson 20 · Surface Code Fundamentals

steps.label: Data qubits sit on a d×d square grid — d² of them
steps.sub: Ancilla (measure) qubits sit at the centers of alternating lattice faces

steps.label: Each ancilla measures one stabilizer on 4 neighboring data qubits
steps.sub: Fewer (2 or 3) at the lattice's boundary

steps.label: Lattice faces checkerboard between X-type and Z-type
steps.sub: Plaquettes vs. vertices — the CSS structure, laid out geometrically

code:
Data qubits:    3x3 grid = 9
Ancilla qubits: d^2 - 1 = 8
Total:          9 + 8 = 17   (matches 2d^2 - 1 = 2(9) - 1 = 17)
caption: 8 distinct stabilizer groupings, alternating X-type and Z-type, cover the 3x3 grid of data qubits exactly.

eyebrow: The verified formulas at larger distances
code:
d=3  -> data 9,   ancilla 8,   total 17
d=5  -> data 25,  ancilla 24,  total 49
d=7  -> data 49,  ancilla 48,  total 97
d=9  -> data 81,  ancilla 80,  total 161
d=11 -> data 121, ancilla 120, total 241
d=15 -> data 225, ancilla 224, total 449
caption: data = d^2, ancilla = d^2-1, total = 2d^2-1 — ancilla count is always exactly one less than data count.

steps.label: Increasing d grows a d×d grid's area quadratically
steps.sub: Total qubit count grows as d², not linearly in d

steps.label: That's why the surface code stays practical at larger d
steps.sub: Even though it needs more qubits than the Steane code at the smallest distance
